qs.q: After the long walk in the hot sun, the children were ___ and asked for something cold to drink.
qs.ex: «thirsty» = צמא. הילדים ביקשו משהו קר לשתות אחרי הליכה בשמש, ולכן הם צמאים. «lazy» (עצלן) אולי מתאים לעייפות, אבל לא מסביר למה ביקשו לשתות.

qs.q: Rina wanted to buy the blue jacket, ___ it was too expensive, so she chose a cheaper one.
qs.ex: «but» = אבל. היא רצתה את המעיל, אבל הוא היה יקר מדי: זה ניגוד בין הרצון למה שקרה. «because» (כי) היה אומר שהיא רצתה אותו בגלל שהוא יקר, וזה לא מתאים לכך שבחרה מעיל זול יותר.

qs.q: The fire spread quickly through the dry forest, and hundreds of families had to ___ their homes in the middle of the night.
qs.ex: «leave» = לעזוב. בגלל השריפה המשפחות נאלצו לעזוב את הבתים באמצע הלילה. «build» (לבנות) או «clean» (לנקות) לא הגיוניים בזמן שריפה בלילה.

qs.q: Please turn off your phones ___ the film, so that other people can enjoy it in silence.
qs.ex: «during» = במהלך. מכבים את הטלפון בזמן הסרט כדי שאחרים יוכלו ליהנות בשקט. «after» (אחרי) לא הגיוני: אחרי הסרט כבר אין צורך בשקט.

qs.q: The small bakery on our street is always busy in the morning, because its bread is fresh and its prices are ___.
qs.ex: «low» = נמוך. המאפייה מלאה אנשים כי הלחם טרי והמחירים נמוכים: שתי סיבות טובות לקנות שם. «high» (גבוה) הוא ההפך, ומחירים גבוהים לא מסבירים למה תמיד יש בה קונים.

qs.q: Lior could not ___ the name of the singer, although he knew every word of her most famous song.
qs.ex: «remember» = לזכור. הוא ידע את כל המילים של השיר, ובכל זאת לא זכר את שם הזמרת: זה הניגוד ש-«although» מבקש. «forget» (לשכוח) לא יוצר ניגוד: «לא יכול היה לשכוח את השם למרות שידע את השיר» לא הגיוני.

qs.q: The streets were still wet this morning, ___ it had rained heavily during the night.
qs.ex: «since» כאן = מכיוון ש. הרחובות רטובים כי ירד גשם בלילה: החלק השני הוא הסיבה. «although» (למרות ש) לא מתאים, כי אין ניגוד בין גשם לרחוב רטוב.

qs.q: Our cat is very ___; she hides under the bed whenever a stranger comes into the house.
qs.ex: «shy» = ביישן. החתולה מתחבאת מתחת למיטה כשאדם זר נכנס, וזה מה שעושה חתול ביישן. «friendly» (ידידותי) הוא ההפך: חתול ידידותי היה ניגש לאורח.

qs.q: Gal finished all his homework; ___, he cleaned his room and helped his father in the garden.
qs.ex: «in addition» = בנוסף. גל סיים שיעורי בית, וחוץ מזה גם ניקה וגם עזר: הוספה של עוד דברים. «however» (עם זאת) דורש ניגוד, ואין כאן ניגוד.

qs.q: The price of tomatoes went up this month, because the cold weather ___ much of the crop in the south.
qs.ex: «damaged» = הזיק, פגע. מזג האוויר הקר פגע בחלק גדול מהיבול, ולכן יש פחות עגבניות והמחיר עלה. «protected» (הגן) הפוך: אם היבול היה מוגן, המחיר לא היה עולה.

qs.q: You can stay at the party ___ ten o'clock, but after that you must come home.
qs.ex: «until» = עד. מותר להישאר עד השעה עשר, ואחרי זה צריך לחזור. «since» (מאז) מתאר זמן שהתחיל בעבר, וזה לא מתאים למשפט על הערב הזה.

qs.q: This bag is too ___ for me to carry alone; can you help me lift it?
qs.ex: «heavy» = כבד. הוא מבקש עזרה להרים את התיק, ולכן התיק כבד מדי. «light» (קל) הוא ההפך: תיק קל לא צריך עזרה.

qs.q: Before the exam, the teacher ___ the students to turn off their phones, because many of them had forgotten to do so the week before.
qs.ex: «remind» = להזכיר. בשבוע הקודם תלמידים רבים שכחו לכבות את הטלפון, ולכן המורה הזכירה להם. «forbade» (אסרה) אומר את ההפך, ו-«allowed» (הרשתה) לא מתאים, כי מי ששכח צריך תזכורת ולא רשות.

qs.q: The beach was closed ___ the strong winds, so we spent the afternoon at the cinema.
qs.ex: «because of» = בגלל. החוף נסגר בגלל הרוחות החזקות, ולכן הלכו לקולנוע. «in spite of» (למרות) לא הגיוני: רוחות חזקות הן סיבה לסגור חוף, לא דבר שמנוגד לסגירה.

qs.q: It is ___ to swim in this river, because the water is deep and moves very fast.
qs.ex: «dangerous» = מסוכן. מים עמוקים וזרם מהיר הופכים את השחייה למסוכנת. «safe» (בטוח) הוא ההפך ממה שהסיבה במשפט מתארת.

qs.q: Yael ___ a lot of money last year by riding her bike to work instead of taking a taxi.
qs.ex: «save» = לחסוך. רכיבה על אופניים במקום מונית עולה פחות, ולכן היא חסכה כסף. «spent» (הוציאה) הפוך: אופניים לא גורמים להוציא הרבה כסף.

qs.q: ___ his long day at work, Avi still went to watch his daughter's school play.
qs.ex: «In spite of» = למרות. אבי היה אחרי יום עבודה ארוך, ובכל זאת הלך להצגה, והמילה «still» (ובכל זאת) מראה שיש כאן ויתור. «Because of» (בגלל) לא הגיוני: יום ארוך הוא לא סיבה ללכת להצגה.

qs.q: The instructions in the box were so ___ that we built the new table in only twenty minutes.
qs.ex: «clear» = ברור. ההוראות היו כל כך ברורות שבנו את השולחן מהר. «confusing» (מבלבל) הפוך: הוראות מבלבלות היו גורמות לעבודה איטית.

qs.q: Many animals sleep through most of the cold winter; bears, ___, may not eat anything for several months.
qs.ex: «for instance» = למשל. הדובים הם דוגמה לבעלי חיים שישנים בחורף. «however» (עם זאת) היה מציג ניגוד, אבל הדובים לא שונים משאר בעלי החיים כאן, הם דוגמה להם.

qs.q: The train was ___ by an hour because of a problem on the tracks, so many passengers were late for work.
qs.ex: «delayed» = התעכב. בגלל בעיה במסילה הרכבת איחרה בשעה, ולכן נוסעים איחרו לעבודה. «repaired» (תוקן) לא מסביר למה הנוסעים איחרו.

qs.q: Shira studied hard all year, ___ she received the highest grade in her class.
qs.ex: «so» = לכן. שירה למדה קשה, ולכן קיבלה את הציון הכי גבוה: החלק השני הוא תוצאה של הראשון. «but» (אבל) מציג ניגוד, ואין ניגוד בין למידה קשה לציון גבוה.

qs.q: The doctor asked Ron to ___ eating sweets for a month to see whether his stomach pains would go away.
qs.ex: «stop» = להפסיק. הרופא רוצה לבדוק אם הכאבים יעברו בלי ממתקים, ולכן ביקש להפסיק לאכול אותם. «continue» (להמשיך) לא יעזור לבדוק את זה.

qs.q: Call me ___ you arrive at the station, and I will come to pick you up right away.
qs.ex: «as soon as» = ברגע ש. כשתגיע לתחנה תתקשר, ואני אבוא מיד. «unless» (אלא אם כן) הופך את המשמעות: «תתקשר אלא אם תגיע» לא הגיוני.

qs.q: Plastic bags are a serious problem for the ___, because they can stay in the sea for hundreds of years.
qs.ex: «environment» = הסביבה. שקיות שנשארות בים מאות שנים פוגעות בטבע ובסביבה. «economy» (כלכלה) או «weather» (מזג האוויר) לא קשורים לזיהום בים.

qs.q: Because the city added more buses to the morning schedule, fewer people now drive their cars to work in the center.
o: Because fewer people drive their cars to work in the center, the city added more buses to the morning schedule.
The city put more buses on the morning schedule; as a result, fewer people drive to work downtown now.
Although the city added more buses in the morning, more people now drive their cars to work in the center.
The city added more buses to the morning schedule, but almost nobody uses them to get to work.
qs.ex: «Because» הוחלף ב-«as a result» (כתוצאה מכך), והסיבה והתוצאה נשארו באותו כיוון: יותר אוטובוסים, ולכן פחות נהגים. התשובה שמתחילה ב-«Because fewer people drive» הופכת את הסיבה והתוצאה.

qs.q: Many older people find it hard to use new phones, so some shops now offer free lessons on Sunday mornings.
o: Many older people find new phones hard to use, although all shops now offer free lessons on Sunday mornings.
Some shops offer free lessons on Sunday mornings, so many older people now find it easy to use new phones.
Many older people teach shop workers how to use new phones during free lessons on Sunday mornings.
Since a lot of older people have difficulty using new phones, several shops now give free classes on Sunday mornings.
qs.ex: «so» (לכן) הפך ל-«Since» (מכיוון ש) בתחילת המשפט, ו-«find it hard» הפך ל-«have difficulty». הקושי של המבוגרים הוא עדיין הסיבה לשיעורים. התשובה עם «all shops» משנה «some» (חלק) ל«כל», ומוסיפה ניגוד שאין במקור.

qs.q: Unlike most birds, penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers and can stay underwater for several minutes while hunting for fish.
o: Most birds can fly, but penguins cannot; still, they swim extremely well and can spend several minutes underwater hunting fish.
Like most other birds, penguins are not able to fly, so they have to stay underwater for several minutes while hunting fish.
Penguins can fly as well as most other birds, and they can also stay underwater for several minutes while they hunt for fish.
Penguins cannot fly, and since they are poor swimmers, they rarely stay underwater for more than a few seconds when hunting fish.
qs.ex: «Unlike most birds» הפך ל-«Most birds can fly, but penguins cannot», «but» הפך ל-«still», ו-«excellent swimmers» ל-«swim extremely well». «Like most other birds» אומר שגם רוב הציפורים לא עפות, וזה הפוך מהמקור.

qs.q: People who live near a park tend to walk more each day than people who live far from green areas.
o: Living near a park makes people walk more each day, because green areas give them more energy.
People who live far from green areas tend to walk more each day than those who live near a park.
Those living close to a park usually walk more every day than those whose homes are far from green spaces.
All people who live near a park walk more each day than anyone who lives far from green areas.
qs.ex: «tend to» (נוטים) הפך ל-«usually» (בדרך כלל): זו נטייה, לא חוק. התשובה עם «makes people walk» מוסיפה שהפארק הוא הסיבה, ו-«All people» הופך נטייה לחוק שתקף לכולם.

qs.q: If you water this plant only once a week, it will grow well even in a small apartment with little sunlight.
o: Watering this plant once a week is enough for it to grow well, even in a small apartment that gets little sun.
This plant will grow well in a small apartment only if it gets a lot of sunlight and water every day.
This plant grows well in a small apartment, but it must be watered several times a week because there is little sunlight.
Even if you water this plant once a week, it will not grow well in a small apartment with little sunlight.
qs.ex: המקור אומר שמספיק להשקות פעם בשבוע, והצמח יגדל טוב גם עם מעט שמש. «is enough» (מספיק) מבטא את «only once a week». התשובה עם «only if it gets a lot of sunlight» סותרת את «little sunlight» שבמקור.

qs.q: Before the new law was passed, drivers could park on this street for free, but now they must pay for every hour.
o: Because drivers had to pay for every hour of parking on this street, a new law now lets them park for free.
Drivers have always had to pay for every hour they park on this street, both before and after the new law.
Before the new law was passed, drivers paid for parking on this street, and now they can park for only one hour.
Drivers used to park on this street at no cost; the new law, however, now requires them to pay for each hour.
qs.ex: «used to» = נהגו בעבר, ו-«at no cost» = «for free». לפני החוק החניה הייתה חינם, ועכשיו משלמים על כל שעה. התשובה «Drivers have always had to pay» אומרת שתמיד שילמו, וזה סותר את המקור.

qs.q: Although the zoo's new elephant house opened only last week, more than ten thousand people have already come to see it.
o: Because the zoo's new elephant house opened last week, fewer than ten thousand people have come to see it so far.
Although more than ten thousand people wanted to see the zoo's new elephant house, it has not opened yet.
The zoo's new elephant house has been open for many years, and ten thousand people visit it every week.
Over ten thousand visitors have already seen the zoo's new elephant house, even though it has been open for just one week.
qs.ex: «Although» הפך ל-«even though» וסדר החלקים התהפך, «more than» הפך ל-«over», ו-«only last week» ל-«just one week». התשובה עם «fewer than» (פחות מ) הופכת את הכמות.

qs.q: Our neighbor rarely leaves his house in the winter, but in the summer he spends almost every evening sitting in the garden.
o: Our neighbor often leaves his house in the winter, and in the summer he also sits in the garden every evening.
In the winter our neighbor seldom goes outside, whereas during the summer he sits in the garden nearly every evening.
Our neighbor rarely sits in the garden in the summer, but in the winter he goes out almost every evening.
Our neighbor rarely leaves his house in the winter because he is ill, but in the summer he feels better.
qs.ex: «rarely» = «seldom» (לעיתים רחוקות), «almost» = «nearly» (כמעט), ו-«but» הפך ל-«whereas». «often» (לעיתים קרובות) הופך את «rarely», והתשובה עם «because he is ill» מוסיפה סיבה שאין במקור.

qs.q: To protect the rare birds that nest near the lake, the city has decided to close the lake path next spring.
o: The city has decided to open a new path by the lake next spring so that visitors can see the rare birds.
Because the rare birds no longer nest near the lake, the city has decided to close the lake path next spring.
Next spring, the path by the lake will be closed by the city so that the rare birds nesting there stay safe.
Bird lovers have asked the city to close the lake path next spring, but the city has decided to keep it open.
qs.ex: המשפט הפך לסביל («will be closed by the city»), ו-«To protect» הפך ל-«so that ... stay safe» (כדי שיהיו מוגנות). המטרה נשארה: להגן על הציפורים. התשובה עם «no longer nest» אומרת שהציפורים כבר לא שם, וזה משנה את הסיבה.

qs.q: Fresh fish should be kept in the fridge and eaten within two days; otherwise, it can make people feel sick.
o: Unless fresh fish is stored in a fridge and eaten in two days or less, it may make people ill.
Fresh fish can still make people feel sick, even if it is kept in the fridge and eaten within two days.
Fresh fish should be eaten within two days, so people who keep it in the fridge often get sick.
Fresh fish can be kept in the fridge for several weeks and still be eaten without making anyone sick.
qs.ex: «otherwise» (אחרת) הפך ל-«Unless» (אלא אם כן): אם לא שומרים במקרר ואוכלים תוך יומיים, הדג עלול להזיק. «within two days» = «in two days or less». התשובה עם «even if» אומרת שהדג מזיק גם כשעושים הכול נכון, וזה הפוך.

qs.q: The new hotel by the beach brought hundreds of jobs to the town; however, it also made the beach much more crowded in summer.
o: Because the beach was too crowded in summer, the town built a new hotel that brought hundreds of jobs.
The new hotel by the beach brought only a few jobs to the town, and the beach is now almost empty in summer.
Although the new beach hotel provided the town with hundreds of jobs, it also led to far bigger summer crowds on the beach.
The new hotel by the beach brought hundreds of jobs to the town, so local people now have more time to enjoy the beach.
qs.ex: «however» הפך ל-«Although» בתחילת המשפט, «brought jobs» ל-«provided ... with jobs», ו-«more crowded» ל-«bigger crowds». גם היתרון וגם החיסרון נשארו. התשובה עם «only a few jobs» משנה את הכמות והופכת את הצפיפות.

qs.q: Children usually learn a second language more easily than adults, especially when they start before the age of ten.
o: Adults usually learn a second language more easily than children, especially if they start before the age of ten.
Learning a second language is generally easier for children than for adults, particularly if they begin before age ten.
All children learn a second language easily, but only if they start studying it before the age of ten.
Children usually learn a second language more easily than adults, because children's teachers are especially patient with them.
qs.ex: «usually» הפך ל-«generally», «especially» ל-«particularly», והמבנה השתנה: «Learning ... is easier for children». התשובה שמתחילה ב-«Adults» הופכת מי לומד בקלות, והאחרונה מוסיפה סיבה (מורים סבלניים) שלא נאמרה.

qs.q: After the flower shop began selling online, the number of its customers doubled, so it now plans to hire more workers.
o: The flower shop began selling online because it had hired more workers and needed twice as many customers.
The flower shop intends to employ additional staff, as it has had twice as many customers since it started selling online.
After the flower shop began selling online, it lost half of its customers, so it plans to let some workers go.
The flower shop has twice as many workers as customers since it started selling its flowers online.
qs.ex: «so» (לכן) הפך ל-«as» (מכיוון ש), «doubled» ל-«twice as many», ו-«hire more workers» ל-«employ additional staff». הסיבה (יותר לקוחות) והתוצאה (עוד עובדים) נשארו. «lost half of its customers» הופך את הנתון.
w: מכיוון ש...; כפי ש...; בזמן ש...

qs.q: Many people believe that cats do not like water, but some kinds of cats actually enjoy swimming and playing in it.
o: It is widely believed that cats dislike water; in fact, certain types of cats like to swim and play in it.
Many people believe that cats enjoy swimming, but in fact most kinds of cats do not like water at all.
All kinds of cats actually enjoy swimming and playing in water, even though many people do not like cats.
Since some kinds of cats enjoy swimming, many people believe that cats should play in water every day.
qs.ex: «Many people believe» הפך לסביל «It is widely believed», «actually» ל-«in fact», ו-«some kinds» ל-«certain types». התשובה עם «All kinds of cats» הופכת «some» (חלק) ל«כל», ומשנה גם את מה שאנשים לא אוהבים.

qs.q: The company let its workers work from home on Fridays, and since then, fewer of them have been late on other weekdays.
o: Because the workers can stay home on Fridays, they are now never late during the rest of the week.
The company let its workers work from home on Fridays because many of them had been late during the week.
Since the company let its workers work from home on Fridays, more of them have been late on other days.
Ever since working from home on Fridays was allowed, fewer employees have come in late on the other weekdays.
qs.ex: המקור מתאר רק מה קרה מאז («since then»): פחות איחורים. «Ever since» (מאז ש) שומר על אותו קשר של זמן, בלי לטעון שזו הסיבה. התשובה עם «Because ... never late» מוסיפה סיבה ומשנה «fewer» (פחות) ל-«never» (אף פעם).

qs.q: Even though the test was short, very few students finished it on time, because the questions were much harder than usual.
o: Because the test was short, most students finished it on time, although the questions were harder than usual.
Very few students finished the test on time, since it was much longer and easier than usual tests.
The questions were far more difficult than normal, so hardly any students completed the test in time, despite its short length.
The test was short and the questions were easier than usual, so very few students needed the whole time to finish it.
qs.ex: «very few» = «hardly any» (כמעט אף אחד), «Even though» הפך ל-«despite» בסוף, ו-«because» הפך ל-«so» עם סדר הפוך. התשובה עם «most students» הופכת את הכמות, והשנייה אומרת שהמבחן ארוך, וזה סותר את המקור.

qs.q: Instead of throwing away old clothes, many families now give them to charity or exchange them with friends and neighbors.
o: Many families now throw away old clothes instead of giving them to charity or to friends and neighbors.
Many families now buy old clothes from charity, and they also sell them to friends and neighbors.
Few families give old clothes to charity, because their friends and neighbors usually throw them away.
Today, many families donate old clothes or swap them with friends and neighbors rather than throw them out.
qs.ex: «Instead of» הפך ל-«rather than» בסוף המשפט, «give to charity» ל-«donate», ו-«exchange» ל-«swap». התשובה הראשונה הופכת את מה שהמשפחות עושות: זורקות במקום לתרום.

qs.q: The village was almost empty during the week, as most of its young people worked in the city and came home only on weekends.
o: Most of the village's young people worked in the city and returned only for weekends, so on weekdays few people were there.
The village was almost empty on weekends, because most of its young people came home from the city only during the week.
Most of the village's young people left the city and moved back home, so the village is no longer empty during the week.
The young people of the village went to work in the city because the village was almost empty during the week.
